title: Passwords: bcrypt, Argon2 and a policy users can actually follow

videos.script: Assume the table of passwords leaks one day. A backup, a stolen laptop, a query that returned too much. {{leak}} The question is what the copy is worth. In plain text, everything. Behind a fast hash, nearly everything: a graphics card guesses billions a second. {{fast}} Behind a slow, salted hash, each guess costs real time and memory, and two patients with the same password look nothing alike. {{slow}} Then the policy. Long beats complicated. A few unrelated words make a good password, and a rule about symbols makes a bad one. {{policy}} Today the portal stores passwords with Argon2, answers a stranger and a wrong password the same way, and ends every other session when a password changes. {{today}}
